articles.title: Saudi Coalition Downs Three Drones North of Riyadh as Sanaa Operation Looms
articles.excerpt: Third day of attacks toward the Saudi capital; the coalition warns civilians out of a Sanaa oil site while Riyadh airport stays shut through Saturday.
articles.image_caption: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The Saudi-led coalition said it downed three drones north of the capital as a Sanaa operation loomed.
articles.nri_angle: Riyadh airport remains closed through October 17 with Indian airlines cancelling Saudi flights, affecting one of the largest Indian expatriate hubs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: White House Asks Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle to Resign Over Misconduct Reports
articles.excerpt: New press secretary Katie Zacharia announced the ouster at her first briefing; Trump said he 'didn't like what I read,' while Guilfoyle denies the allegations.
articles.image_caption: Kimberly Guilfoyle is pictured in a close-up portrait. The White House asked her to resign as US ambassador to Greece on Tuesday following reports alleging misconduct.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Energy Department Declares Grid Emergency Across PJM's 13 States as Demand Squeezes Supply
articles.excerpt: Emergency Order 202-26-50 runs October 13–16 for the PJM Interconnection, which serves about 65 million people. PJM has issued an Energy Emergency Alert Level 1 for October 13, with demand expected near 111,500 MW amid warm weather and generator maintenance — no regionwide rolling blackouts have been announced.
articles.image_caption: High-voltage electric power transmission lines. The US Energy Department declared a grid emergency across PJM's 13 states as demand squeezed supply.
articles.nri_angle: PJM's territory covers major Indian-American population centres in New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Illinois and Ohio — households there should follow their local utility's conservation requests through October 16.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'His Father Will Handle Everything': Family of Kochi Crash Victim Fears Case Is Being Weakened
articles.excerpt: Three 21-year-old students — Iyas, Devika and Gopika — were killed when a Mini Cooper rammed their scooter near Nedumbassery on October 11. Gopika's father alleges the accused's family is using its influence, and questions why the 19-year-old driver was sent to a borstal school.
articles.image_caption: Kochi, Kerala. The family of a Kochi crash victim fears the case against the accused is being weakened.
articles.nri_angle: The crash near Kochi's international airport has become a test of whether Kerala's justice system treats a wealthy young accused the same as anyone else — a question Malayali families abroad are following closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Courted by Both Parties, Indian-American Voters Head Into Midterms Leaning Democratic — and Independent
articles.excerpt: A summer AAPI survey puts Democratic House candidates ahead 66% to 18% among Indian-American voters, while Carnegie's data shows independents climbing to 29% — the bloc both parties are now fighting over.
articles.nri_angle: With 92% of Indian-American registered voters planning to vote on November 3, the community's growing independent streak makes it a genuine swing constituency in close House and Senate races.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Drone Attack Sinks Ship Off Bulgaria, Second Strike in a Week
articles.excerpt: The Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3 was damaged and its 15 crew rescued after three drone hits near the Bulgarian coast, as Sofia summons Russia's ambassador and seeks talks with NATO.
articles.image_caption: The Black Sea. A drone attack sank a ship off Bulgaria, the second strike in a week.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian readers abroad, the attacks underline how the Russia-Ukraine war is widening risks for global shipping routes that carry fuel and food to markets worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nithya Raman Takes 11-Point Lead Over Karen Bass Into Only LA Mayoral Debate
articles.excerpt: A Berkeley IGS/Los Angeles Times poll puts the Indian-American councilmember ahead 39% to 28% — but with 33% of voters undecided and mail ballots already out, the October 14 debate is the race's biggest moment.
articles.image_caption: Los Angeles Councilmember Nithya Raman at her office. Raman leads Mayor Karen Bass by 11 points in the latest Berkeley IGS poll ahead of their October 14 debate.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-born councilmember leads the incumbent mayor of Los Angeles three weeks before the runoff — a first-tier diaspora candidacy in America's second-largest city.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Only live televised debate between Raman and Bass

articles.title: Ranjeev Puri Could Become the First Indian American State House Speaker in the US
articles.excerpt: Michigan's House Democratic leader needs a Democratic flip on November 3 and a caucus vote to make history — as both parties court the state's Indian-American voters.
articles.image_caption: The Michigan State Capitol in Lansing. Representative Ranjeev Puri could become the first Indian American state House speaker in the US.
articles.nri_angle: A Sikh American son of Punjabi immigrants is one election and one caucus vote from a Speaker's gavel no Indian American has ever held.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Puri must win re-election on November 3.
Democrats need a majority in the Michigan House.
Puri's caucus must elect him as Speaker.

articles.title: Trump Says Putin Wants a Deal More Than Zelenskyy, Presses Kyiv to Settle
articles.excerpt: The president defended his disputed energy-ceasefire claim and put the onus on Ukraine's leader, while Kyiv reported fresh Russian strikes and European leaders publicly backed Zelenskyy.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump. Trump said Vladimir Putin wants a deal more than Volodymyr Zelenskyy and pressed Kyiv to settle.
articles.nri_angle: The disputed ceasefire and the Russian diesel deal feed directly into the fuel prices and energy security that Indian households and importers are already paying for.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IMF Warns an AI Share Crash Could Test the Limits of Global Resilience
articles.excerpt: The Fund's stability report flags $650 billion of AI-linked debt, circular financing between tech giants and surging hyperscaler bond issuance as vulnerabilities that could turn an earnings miss into a global selloff.
articles.image_caption: The International Monetary Fund headquarters in Washington. The IMF warned an AI-driven share crash could test global financial resilience.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora portfolios are concentrated in US tech; the IMF says an AI correction would hit the US and Asian markets hardest, with leverage amplifying any selloff.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Netanyahu Sought Saudi Approval to Join Houthi Strikes; Riyadh Said No
articles.excerpt: Working through US mediators, Israel's prime minister asked to join the campaign against Yemen's Houthis — partly to advance normalisation — but Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman opposed direct Israeli participation, according to Haaretz.
articles.image_caption: Flames and smoke rise from an airport terminal next to a Saudi Arabian Airlines aircraft after a Houthi strike in Saudi Arabia. The repeated attacks on Saudi airports prompted Netanyahu's request for Israel to join the campaign against the Houthis.
articles.nri_angle: Houthi strikes have already killed an Indian national at Riyadh airport and threaten the Red Sea trade route and Gulf airspace that millions of Indian workers and travellers depend on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Global Trade Passing Through Bab el-Mandeb
Indian National Killed in Houthi Attack

articles.title: Lehigh Valley Indian Americans Celebrate Diwali at Saucon Valley High School
articles.excerpt: The Indian American Association of Lehigh Valley held its annual Diwali celebration on October 10 in Hellertown, an open-to-all day of performances, food and community run by the volunteer non-profit founded in 1972.
articles.image_caption: Performers dance on stage during the Indian American Association of Lehigh Valley Diwali celebration at Saucon Valley High School in Hellertown. The event is one of the association's flagship annual cultural celebrations in Pennsylvania's Lehigh Valley.
articles.nri_angle: A volunteer association founded in 1972 still anchors Diwali for Indian Americans across Pennsylvania's Lehigh Valley, opening the celebration to the whole region.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Times Square Durga Utsav Draws Crowds Despite Bad Weather, Honours Six Organisations
articles.excerpt: The second annual Sharadiya Durgotsav filled Father Duffy Square with ritual, dance and music on October 10-11, and recognised six diaspora organisations that have sustained Durga Puja in the US for over 50 years.
articles.image_caption: A Durga idol during Durga Puja celebrations. The second annual Sharadiya Durga Utsav was held at Father Duffy Square in Times Square on October 10-11.
articles.nri_angle: A Bengali festival staged in the middle of Manhattan shows how the diaspora is moving its biggest celebrations into America's most public spaces.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Six organizations honored for 50+ years of service.
Dhunuchi dance symbolizes victory over evil.

articles.title: Moosewala Returns to a Toronto Stage as a Hologram as Toddler Brother Recreates His Thaapi
articles.excerpt: The 'Signed to God' hologram tour opened to a packed Scotiabank Arena, where two-year-old Shubhdeep's thaapi became the night's defining moment. US dates follow in New York, Houston and Oakland.
articles.image_caption: Sidhu Moose Wala, the Punjabi singer whose hologram performed in Toronto, with his toddler brother recreating his signature thaapi gesture.
articles.nri_angle: Toronto's Punjabi diaspora was Moosewala's second home market; the tour continues to Vancouver and Calgary, then New York, Houston and Oakland for US fans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Riyadh Airport Closure Extended as Saudi Arabia Tracks New Drone, Missile Threats
articles.excerpt: Saudi civil aviation extended the King Khalid International Airport suspension with no reopening date, as the coalition tracked a fresh drone and cruise missile threat and probed how the weekend strikes got through.
articles.image_caption: A missile is launched in a screen grab from footage released by the Houthis' Ansarullah Media Centre. Saudi Arabia extended the Riyadh airport closure on Monday as it tracked a fresh drone and cruise missile threat.
articles.nri_angle: Indian carriers have cancelled Saudi services through October 15 and the Indian embassy's stay-indoors advisory remains the reference point for the large Indian workforce in the kingdom.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zelenskyy Says Russia Struck Energy Sites Hours After Trump Announced Ceasefire
articles.excerpt: Ukraine held its fire overnight, Zelenskyy told Fox News, while a strike on a Kharkiv power plant killed three. Moscow has not confirmed it accepted any energy ceasefire.
articles.image_caption: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Zelenskyy said Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure continued hours after Trump announced an energy ceasefire.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Riyadh Airport Hit Again as US and Allies Warn Travellers Away From Saudi Airports
articles.excerpt: A second strike in two days killed one person at King Khalid International Airport and Dammam's airport was also targeted, as Trump weighs joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis and Western governments tell citizens to avoid Saudi airports.
articles.nri_angle: With Indian airlines already extending Saudi cancellations and thousands of Indian workers transiting Gulf hubs, travellers should check flight status before heading to any Saudi airport and follow Indian Embassy advisories.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Family of Hyderabad Man Killed in Riyadh Airport Attack Will Hold Funeral in Saudi Arabia
articles.excerpt: Mohammed Yousuf Ali, 46, was killed travelling to Medina for Umrah. The Indian Embassy says it is completing funeral formalities in Riyadh while five injured Indians remain in intensive care.
articles.nri_angle: For the large Indian workforce in Saudi Arabia, the embassy's hospital-by-hospital updates and funeral assistance are the front line of support; families in India should route queries through the Indian Embassy in Riyadh.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Left a $200,000 Microsoft Job for an AI Startup. Revenue So Far: $6,000.
articles.excerpt: Seattle-based Junead Khan traded a ₹1.9 crore Microsoft package for Treasury, an AI money coach — living on savings, building solo with AI tools, and documenting every failed launch.
articles.image_caption: Junead Khan with a laptop for his AI startup Treasury, beside a Microsoft campus sign. Khan left a Microsoft job that paid over $200,000 a year to build Treasury, which has generated more than $6,000 in revenue so far.
articles.nri_angle: A diaspora entrepreneur's playbook: bank big-tech earnings as seed funding, time exits around vesting cliffs and bonus repayment windows — but visa-holders should consult an immigration attorney before quitting, since an H-1B is tied to the employer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Witnesses Say Tiger Victim Posed for Photos, Danced Before Entering Enclosure
articles.excerpt: Witnesses say the man asked a stranger to photograph him with the tiger Altai in the background minutes before climbing over the barrier at Yorkshire Wildlife Park.
articles.image_caption: An Amur tiger. The victim posed for photos with Altai the tiger before entering the enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park.
articles.nri_angle: A UK wildlife-park tragedy with a lesson for Indian families in Britain: viewing barriers are there for a reason, and young visitors should never be unsupervised near large-animal enclosures.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Panama Declares Emergency as 200+ Aftershocks Follow 7.7 Quake
articles.excerpt: With no deaths reported but at least 27 injured and nearly 900 homes damaged, Panama's national emergency unlocks up to $100 million in relief as scientists record more than 200 aftershocks since Friday's 7.7-magnitude quake.
articles.image_caption: Earthquake damage in Panama. The country declared a national state of emergency after more than 200 aftershocks.
articles.nri_angle: Panama's small Indian community in Colón's Zona Libre and Panama City faces no reported casualties; diaspora readers with family, business, or travel plans in Veraguas and Los Santos should expect disrupted roads and check advisories before departure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Telangana Woman, 31, Dies in Missouri Crash; Toddler Left Behind
articles.excerpt: Daram Supriya was returning home in Wentzville after closing the St. Louis restaurant she ran when a truck struck her car from behind; her family has appealed for help bringing her remains back to India.
articles.nri_angle: A Telangana mother's death in Missouri leaves a grieving family navigating repatriation and a 2.5-year-old child — with a GoFundMe campaign set up in Supriya's name and her father's appeal to the Telangana government for help bringing her home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Saritha Komatireddy Challenges Letitia James for New York Attorney General
articles.excerpt: The first South Asian major-party nominee for statewide office in New York is taking on one of the state's most powerful Democrats — and the polls are tightening ahead of the November 3 election.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian American is on New York's statewide ballot for the first time — and the November 3 result will measure how far South Asian representation has come in the state's top offices.

articles.title: Shikhar Mohan: The 21-Year-Old Ranchi Opener Making Himself Count
articles.excerpt: 613 Ranji runs at 55.73, twin fifties in the Duleep final, and a nod from Shahbaz Nadeem — Jharkhand's 21-year-old left-hander is forcing his way into the conversation.
articles.image_caption: Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan poses with his bat during a training session. The 21-year-old left-hander was Jharkhands highest run-getter in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy season.
articles.nri_angle: With India's top order in generational transition, domestic run-machines like Mohan are who selectors watch — diaspora fans who track the Ranji Trophy's breakout names should know his.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Played at No. 3, not usual opening slot

articles.title: Kamini Ramani's 'Lotus Leadership' Asks: Where Are the Indian American Women?
articles.excerpt: Silicon Valley executive Kamini Ramani's new book argues that Indian American women succeeded by drawing on their heritage — not by imitating men or 'leaning in.'
articles.image_caption: Lotus flowers. Kamini Ramani's Lotus Leadership: A Modern Playbook of Ancient Wisdom, published by HarperCollins, distills a year of interviews with more than 30 Indian-heritage women leaders in American business into a 'Five Petals' framework.
articles.nri_angle: A new book documents how Indian American women built extraordinary business careers on their own terms — essential reading for the next generation of diaspora professionals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: The Five Petals of Lotus Leadership

articles.title: Drone Strikes Tanker Carrying 11 Indian Seafarers Off Oman; Two Missing
articles.excerpt: The Nicaragua-flagged MT Petro Dolphin was hit at Sohar Anchorage on Sunday; nine of its 11 Indian crew were rescued as Oman's Coast Guard searches for two missing sailors.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea (file photo) — the Nicaragua-flagged MT Petro Dolphin, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, was struck by a drone at Sohar Anchorage off Oman on October 11.
articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers face the sharpest edge of the Gulf shipping attacks; the Indian Embassy in Muscat is coordinating rescue efforts and consular help for the affected crews and their families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Flash Flood Devastates Villages in Nepal's Gorkha, Bridges Swept Away as 10 Go Missing
articles.excerpt: A sudden surge in the Budhi Gandaki river swept away settlements, six bridges and a hydropower project in Gorkha district; the army and helicopters have been deployed as 10 people remain missing.
articles.image_caption: A village in Nepal's Gorkha district. A flash flood devastated villages there, sweeping away bridges and homes as 10 went missing.
articles.nri_angle: Nepal's diaspora in the US, Gulf and Australia will be checking on family in Gorkha; the region also draws Indian trekkers and pilgrims, and Indian authorities often coordinate relief with Kathmandu.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Navratri Begins: Celebrating Nine Nights of Devotion and Joy
articles.excerpt: Join the vibrant festivities of Navratri, honoring the divine feminine.
articles.image_caption: Revellers perform garba with dandiya sticks during Navratri, the nine-night festival of devotion and joy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IRGC Says Supertanker Struck Mine and Exploded Trying to Exit Strait of Hormuz
articles.excerpt: The Revolutionary Guards said the vessel was sailing dark, with navigation systems switched off, through a route Tehran had declared high-risk; the vessel was not identified and the account has not been independently verified.
articles.image_caption: Small boats and ships navigate waters in the Gulf region. A supertanker struck a mine and caught fire while trying to exit the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state-linked claims that remain unverified.
articles.nri_angle: India imports the bulk of its crude, so a Strait of Hormuz disruption lands directly on fuel prices watched by NRI households, and thousands of Indian seafarers crew the tankers transiting the waterway.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: Impact of Strait of Hormuz Disruption

articles.title: All 22 Indian Crew Safe After Tanker MT GEM No.2 Attacked Off UAE Coast
articles.excerpt: The fully laden Panama-flagged tanker was struck at anchor off the UAE on Friday, sparking a fire; New Delhi says it is in direct contact with the ship's managers while seafarers' unions demand stronger protection for Indian crews.
articles.image_caption: A crude oil tanker at anchor (file photo). The Panama-flagged MT GEM No.2, a 302,000-tonne vessel, was struck by an unidentified projectile in UAE waters on October 9; all 22 Indian crew members are safe.
articles.nri_angle: The UAE hosts one of the world's largest Indian expatriate communities and Indian nationals form a large share of global seafaring crews, making a strike on an all-Indian-crewed tanker a direct diaspora-safety story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
